body:
Good Friday morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a remarkable one: a local CHP widow's "Tips for Chips" fundraiser has now passed $590,000 raised for the families of fallen officers. Outside, expect a mild November day — a high near 72, a low around 52 tonight, air quality sitting at a moderate 74, and no active weather alerts or fires anywhere in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

It was a busy night for Bakersfield police, with two weapons calls and three burglary reports landing in the early hours. The most serious came at 1:27 a.m., when officers were sent to the 4,200 block of Actis Street in southwest Bakersfield for a physical fight between a man and his girlfriend; the woman was reported to be trying to stab him. A second weapons call followed at 2:51 a.m. at Beale Park on Oleander Avenue, where a woman was reported to be near the restrooms with two men who had bats and knives, and dispatchers were told a sexual assault was possible. Earlier, at 2:02 a.m., officers went to North Meadows Park on McCray Street, where a woman had a facial injury after an argument with her ex-boyfriend.

Burglaries kept officers moving too. A woman watching her home camera called at 1:47 a.m. to report men walking into her garage on the 2,100 block of Bedford Way in north Bakersfield, one of them believed to have a pistol. A man dropped onto a property from a roof on China Grade Loop at 12:21 a.m., and a business on the 400 block of East 19th Street was hit at 2:04 a.m. Two chases crossed the night — a reckless blue pickup on Pike Street at 8:45 p.m., and a car that stopped on Castro Lane near Rose Marie Drive around 1:08 a.m., its occupants running before officers caught up with them. Fire crews had nothing larger than grass and field fires, a cart alight on State Road and an outside fire on Wisteria Street.

One more note from the log: at 4:44 a.m., officers were sent to the Chevron on the 3,100 block of Niles Street, where a caller was standing by with a boy about 10 or 11 years old who was possibly autistic. An alert for a missing 9-year-old boy had gone out on Oswell Street.

## Today's weather

It's 52 degrees right now at Meadows Field, and we're headed to a high near 72 this afternoon — about as pleasant as early November gets in the valley. Tonight's low settles around 52 again. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and no active fires to report. Air quality is 74, which lands in the moderate range, so if you're sensitive to particulates, it's a reasonable day to keep an eye on how you feel during longer stretches outside. Otherwise, expect a calm, clear Friday — good conditions for the football playoffs tonight and for anything you've got planned outdoors this weekend.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that a Bakersfield CHP widow's annual fundraiser has now raised more than $590,000 for the families of officers killed in the line of duty.** Shannon Ehly lost her husband, CHP Officer Mark Ehly, in 2010, and months later West Side Rotary's Jim Darling approached her about starting "Tips for Chips" in his honor. The event puts CHP officers to work serving food and drinks, with proceeds going to the CHP Widows and Orphans Trust Fund — the same fund that once sent Ehly's own family a check. This year's edition alone brought in more than $58,000, and Ehly told the station the real power of the night is a community that keeps showing up.

**According to 23ABC, students from Bakersfield Christian High School took the stage Thursday night at a TEDx Youth event at Stockdale Christian School to share their struggles and hopes with an adult audience.** The school's director of academic programs, Ashley Pavletich, said the school rallied behind the students to make sure the event could happen. Senior Mariana Vargas organized it, telling the station it matters that young people know they aren't alone and that there are people willing to guide them and understand what they're going through. One student, Brody Pierce, made the case plainly: teenagers experience just as much as adults, just in a different way.

**KGET 17 reports that public memorials are being scheduled in Bakersfield for Dolores Huerta.** The station has not yet shared full details of the services, but the announcement marks a significant moment for a community with deep ties to the labor and civil rights leader's life and work. We'll pass along times and locations as they're confirmed.

**23ABC reports that a Bakersfield caregiver was sentenced Thursday in an elder abuse case that began with a Ring camera video that went viral on social media.** Julie Joleen Rothgeb received one year of probation, including 60 days in jail, 480 hours of supervised community service and a five-year stay-away order after a judge found her guilty of one misdemeanor count of elder abuse and four misdemeanor counts of battery. The case dates to June 2025, when footage appeared to show Rothgeb mistreating Diane, a woman now 70. Diane's daughter, Windy Dueñas, told the station she kept pushing for accountability after her first report to authorities went nowhere, and the family delivered victim impact statements at Thursday's sentencing. Rothgeb's public defender, Ryan Fallgatter, said he respects the judge's finding but maintains a change in her anxiety medication played a role.

**Bakersfield Now reports that the Stockdale Highway off-ramp will close permanently on Nov. 20.** Drivers who use that exit regularly should start thinking now about an alternate route, because once it's gone, it's gone. We'll have more on what the closure means for daily commutes as the date approaches.

**KGET 17 has posted its preview and predictions for the opening round of the 2026 CIF Central Section football playoffs here in Kern County.** If you're heading to a game tonight, it's worth a look before you go — the station breaks down the matchups and picks its winners. High school playoff football under Friday night lights is one of the valley's best traditions, and this week's slate looks like a good one.

## Something good

CSUB has unveiled a new Hispanic cultural center, adding a dedicated space on campus for Hispanic culture and community. It's the kind of room that matters long after the ribbon is cut — a place for students to gather, celebrate and see themselves reflected in the university they call home. Congratulations to everyone who worked to make it happen.

And one more reason to smile: Thursday night's TEDx Youth event was organized entirely by a high school senior, with her classmates stepping up to share some genuinely hard personal stories in front of a room full of adults. Whatever you think about teenagers, that took nerve.

## Coming up this week

It's a full weekend at the Fox Theater. Journey USA takes the stage Saturday, Nov. 7, and the Texas Tornado Tradition — Tex-Mex classics with some new sounds, per KGET 17 — plays the Fox the same night. On Sunday, Nov. 8, the 2026 Golden Empire Youth Cheer EXPO brings the valley's young cheer squads together at the Fox, and Monday, Nov. 9, the Cults & Classics series screens "Play Misty for Me." Looking further out, NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet arrives Nov. 13, and season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are already on sale.

On the public meeting side, the Fire Civil Service Commission meets Monday, Nov. 9, at 3 p.m. If you've got business with that commission, mark your calendar now. And a reminder for drivers: the Stockdale Highway off-ramp closes permanently Nov. 20, so this is a good week to test out the route you'll use instead.

Have a good Friday, Bakersfield.

top.title: CHP widow's 'Tips for Chips' fundraiser has raised more than $590,000
